sections.html:
Wilson County Tax Administration lists, values and collects property tax for the county. It also collects for nine municipalities, two solid waste taxes, two special districts and fifteen fire districts, so one bill can carry several layers. Details are on the tax administration page.

The counter is at 113 Nash Street East in the city of Wilson, and there are four ways to pay, online among them. Bills go out by mail in early August. Owners of residential dwellings outside a municipality now get a solid waste permit with that bill.

Mail is processed by the USPS postmark. A drop box or a small post office may not stamp the same day, so send payments, listing forms and appeals several days early or ask the counter clerk for a postmark.

sections.h2: Wilson County housing at a glance
sections.html:
The county covers roughly 373 square miles east of Raleigh. Its seat, the city of Wilson, has more than 50,000 residents on about 14.2 square miles, and the county carries roughly 43,000 parcels in its real estate listing system.

  • 81,150 people, a 2.4% rise since the 2020 count.
  • 38,463 housing units, with owners living in 60.0% of occupied homes.
  • Typical owned homes valued at $186,000 and typical rent of $953.

Six in ten occupied homes have owner residents, so most of your buyers will be buying to live in the house, while a sizable minority of sellers are landlords.

Bills fall due September 1. Payment at face amount works up to the day before January 6, and balances left after that are delinquent.

Late interest begins at 2% for the first weeks and then climbs by three-fourths of a percent each month. Ask the tax office whether any early payment discount applies, since a county may adopt a discount schedule by a resolution passed before May 1.

One common seller question has a simple answer. The person on the deed as of January 1 receives the bill, and a later sale usually changes the name only for the following year.

Wilson County reappraised real property as of January 1, 2024, its first reappraisal since 2016, and it works on an eight year cycle. North Carolina law requires counties to reappraise at least that often.

The revaluation covered more than 41,000 real property parcels. Personal property has been split onto its own bill, apart from real estate, since the 2024 bills.

The county's Comper tool lets an owner compare a house with neighborhood sales as of the revaluation date. Those sales are the best evidence to bring to the tax office if a value looks high.

Get the current form and cutoff from the tax office. Each real property window closes when the review board adjourns, and a new one opens the following January.

State law sets the outer frame. The commissioners normally sit as the review board in spring, and an owner who loses at that stage has a month to go on to the state commission.

Personal property has its own appeal cutoff, set each year. The appeal has to be in writing, by email or postmarked by that deadline, so ask the tax office for the date before you rely on it. Keep a copy of whatever you send, and note the postmark date.

Three state relief programs exist, and one owner draws on only one of them. The county tax office takes the application, and the state AV-9 form names June 1 as the cutoff.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: shelters the larger of $25,000 or half a home's appraised value for older or fully disabled owners under the income ceiling, printed by NCDOR as $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: removes $45,000 of value for a qualifying disabled veteran, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: holds the bill to 4% or 5% of income, with the $58,200 ceiling, and defers the rest as a lien.

The rules are on the NCDOR form.

sections.h2: What else can appear on the bill
sections.html:
Besides the county levy, a parcel may carry a municipal tax, a fire district tax, a special district tax or a solid waste charge, because the county collects for all of them. Which ones apply depends on where the house stands, so read the bill line by line. If a line surprises you, call the tax office before closing so the buyer is not caught off guard by a charge that was never mentioned.

A seller with a vehicle, boat or business equipment may receive two separate bills, since personal property is billed apart from real estate. For homes outside a municipality, the solid waste permit arrives with the annual bill, so a buyer taking over such a house should ask the seller to hand it over at closing.

A house inside the city of Wilson is billed for city tax through the same office, and the tax calculator on the county site lets owners test the combined result with their assessed value.

A balance follows the parcel into the sale, so closing is the moment to clear it. The lien arises on the listing date each year, and collection can end in a court-supervised sale.

Wilson County adds a local step. Under G.S. 161-31 and a 2004 commissioners' resolution, the Register of Deeds takes a deed for recording only if it carries a statement about delinquent taxes. An attorney can complete the statement personally, or the deed goes first to the Collections Division of the tax department, where a clerk checks the parcel for delinquent tax. The county asks that taxes and recording fees go in separate checks. Questions go to the tax office at 252-399-2900, option 2.

Wilson County property tax calendar
StepTiming
Value and owner fixedJanuary 1
Listing periodJanuary 1 to 31 (extensions possible)
Relief applicationsThrough June 1
Taxes dueSeptember 1
Face amount payment endsDay before January 6

If your closing falls in the fall, the settlement agent should show the bill as paid or credit it from your proceeds.

1. Call 252-399-2900, option 2, and ask for the balance on your parcel.
  2. Decide with your attorney which route you will use for the delinquent tax statement.
  3. Write two checks, one for taxes and one for recording fees.
  4. Ask for the solid waste permit hand-off, if the house is outside a city.

A cash buyer still needs the deed recorded with that statement, so a clean tax account shortens the closing no matter how the buyer pays.

faqs.q: How can I send a payment to the Wilson County tax office?
faqs.a: Visit the counter at 113 Nash Street East in Wilson, or use the county's online payment site. Four payment methods are offered in all.

faqs.q: Who receives the bill if I sell during the year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner. A mid-year sale normally shows up the next tax year, so buyer and seller settle the split at closing.

faqs.q: Is the Wilson County cutoff January 5 or January 6?
faqs.a: January 6 is the last day, and par payment is allowed before January 6. Confirm the exact cutoff with the tax office before you pay late in the season.

faqs.q: Is an appeal still open to me?
faqs.a: Ask the tax office, because the window depends on the year. Real property windows close when the review board adjourns, and a new one opens the next January.

faqs.q: Do I need a clearance before recording a deed in Wilson County?
faqs.a: Yes, in the sense that the deed needs a delinquent tax statement. An attorney can sign it, or a tax department clerk can verify the parcel first, and the Register of Deeds then records it.
